chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ubayd Allah al-Dihqan, from Durust, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Six things in which the servants have no agency: knowledge, ignorance, contentment, anger, sleep, and wakefulness.
ai.seo_question: What are the six things humans have no control over according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates six innate states—knowledge, ignorance, contentment, anger, sleep, and wakefulness—where human volition (*san'*) is absent, highlighting the interplay between divine decree (*qadar*) and natural disposition. This classification underscores the Shia theological distinction between actions fully under human control and those governed by God’s will or physiological necessity, serving as a foundation for understanding moral responsibility. The mention of 'knowledge' and 'ignorance' specifically points to the innate capacity for recognition (*ma'rifah*) which, while divinely granted, is actualized through spiritual effort.
